text:
That is my goal -- also it's a reference point for prior moves so I can go back to see how they played out. As I've said before some keep a private journal / notion / Evernote etc. but mine for the most part is just public. I often go back and review moves just like I did when I said $SMX = $RGC yesterday - same set up same result.

Some look at it as "told ya so" but reality is there is no GOOD WAY to share the information w/ out coming across that way. I could keep it private or, in this case, you can always go back and review charts and concepts to see how they play out. It's record keeping to see how I traded things or how things reacted in the past. Many times, it's the same or very close to it.

Those that take it as 'hindsight' (even though they can see time stamps and it's real time in @IUTraders that's not the point) They miss out on the broader goal of storing things in one place for easy access later. More often than not people ask "what does this ticker remind you of?" and I can quickly search my feed and pull up the chart on that day and even how I likely traded it.

It helps with ticker recall, helps w/ understanding potential range etc. It's never about being right/wrong it's about compiling the best historical information to use for the next trade. Those that focus on reverse engineering find immense help in it, those who focus on other stuff just miss out!

While there is some truth to what you posted I think it'd be hard to say the writing hasn't been on the wall for this week. Starting w/ $SMX - I think a good follow is @TradetheMatrix1 as well for getting a sense of market flow as well risk on risk off. A lot of times our ideas of outlier markets sync extremely well. In fact a lot of times you see him say same thing as me moments later or vice versa I say same thing as him moments later.

Point is $SMX is the start of the move. So one should ASSUME and not be SURPRISED that this market follows. Then, you had low volume traps -- EVERY SINGLE stock that has gone crazy has NOT breached VWAP (if it has it was only for a candle). To me, the writing is right in front of you (speaking to any small cap traders).

It's not that it's rigged against you - it's not about "nailing" the plays it's about knowing when to put risk on risk off -- OR just sit it out. Sitting it out is a win too.

The more squeezes in a row the MORE it trains LONGS to get long and "TRUST" the move so shorts have a harder time because ZERO sellers. But, as this trend continues the scale tips and BUYERS are the crowd not shorts ie: $MIGI this AM etc. looking for replication of the rest.

But, one thing to consider is just look at EVERY name small cap traders had a hard time with.

Now, look how much meat was on the back side.

I think your tweet respectfully makes it overcomplicated -- edge is just about identifying when the market rewards faders and tape is thick vs. when it's trading the same volume but when you go for your exit it's thin as hell. This has been clear - crystal clear for 1.5 weeks or more.

To simplify it further -> being able to get a feel for RISK ON vs. RISK OFF = the TRUE edge over any "concepts" or "strategies"

Knowing when scale tips in your favor.

Knowing when the scale is teetering. This week scale has been teetering both ways but yet people still put RISK ON short side in an environment that is supporting RISK ON long side.

But, does that mean don't short? No, not at all. But, take a step back - macro view HOW MUCH MORE MEAT WAS LEFT AFTER IT CRACKED. AFTER IT REBOUNDED AND FAILED. AFTER SHORTS GOT STUCK.

But yet most are afraid to miss the top.

$TWG $TGL $BBGI etc.

Reward all longs over and over -- scale tips longs stuck - back side massive.

Now we are approaching "chase it all" RISK ON and likely teetering LONG > SHORT crowd ie: $MIGI etc.

Even $BTTC this morning show me a VWAP breach that makes sense to short? Show me a reason for longs to sell.

Quite simply if you were LONG and you missed your exit and were waiting for the bounce to sell, and it DIDN'T bounce, where would you sell? That's when I first get interested in a short.
